items.prompt:
Invented weekly figures for the fictional Etosha Cloth Workshop in Namibia. Fixed cost: N$120. Total variable cost: N$180. Weekly output: 30 cloth bags. Selling price: N$14 per bag. All 30 bags are sold.

Calculate total cost and average cost for the supplied week. Show the formula, substitution and units.
items.canonical_answer: TC = FC + VC = N$120 + N$180 = N$300 per week. AC = TC/Q = N$300/30 = N$10 per bag.
marking_guidance: Formula and substitution/working (1): TC = 120 + 180 = N$300 per week. Formula, result and units/interpretation (1): AC = 300/30 = N$10 per bag, the cost per unit. Total 2.

facts: Invented weekly figures for the fictional Etosha Cloth Workshop in Namibia. Fixed cost: N$120. Total variable cost: N$180. Weekly output: 30 cloth bags. Selling price: N$14 per bag. All 30 bags are sold.

items.prompt:
Invented weekly figures for the fictional Etosha Cloth Workshop in Namibia. Fixed cost: N$120. Total variable cost: N$180. Weekly output: 30 cloth bags. Selling price: N$14 per bag. All 30 bags are sold.

Analyse why an average-cost figure should not be interpreted as the total weekly cost. Use the supplied data to establish the figures you need.
items.canonical_answer: Average cost is N$10 for each bag while total weekly cost is N$300 for all 30 bags. Multiplying the average by 30 recovers the total. The two figures answer different questions, so a lower average does not by itself establish a fall in total cost when output changes.
marking_guidance: Relationship/pattern (1): average cost is cost per unit, total cost covers the whole output. Evidence/comparison (1): N$10 per bag versus N$300 for 30 bags. Explanation/reason (2): multiply average by quantity to recover total (1), so output must also be considered when comparing totals (1). Total 4.
